extracted.intended_audience: early-career biomedical and chemistry faculty (potential applicants), university nominating officials, research administrators
extracted.subtask_description: Eligibility and basic award terms for the Searle Scholars Program: who may be nominated, what fields and career stage are targeted, how many awards are made each year, and the award amount/duration. This is guidance for prospective applicants and institutional nominators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program goal
rubrics_metrics.description: The goal of the award is to support to exceptional young scientists who are at the beginning of their independent research careers and are working in the fields of medicine, chemistry, and/or biological sciences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Searle Scholars Program is described as a career development award made annually to support 15 young faculty in biomedical research and chemistry at US universities and research centers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligible fields
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must be pursuing independent research careers in biochemistry, cell biology, genetics, immunology, neuroscience, pharmacology, and related areas in chemistry, medicine, and the biological sciences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page lists specific disciplinary areas (biochemistry, cell biology, genetics, immunology, neuroscience, pharmacology) and allows related areas in chemistry, medicine, and biological sciences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Career-stage eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must be in their first or second year of their first tenure-track assistant professor position.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This requirement restricts the program to very early-career faculty who have recently started independent, tenure-track assistant professor appointments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional nomination eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants at 176 universities are eligible to be nominated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nomination is limited to applicants from a defined set of eligible institutions (the page notes 176 universities are eligible), implying institutional nomination processes and limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Number of awards per year
rubrics_metrics.description: The award is made annually to support 15 young faculty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The program selects approximately fifteen scholars each year (annual cohort size).

rubrics_metrics.name: Award amount and payment schedule
rubrics_metrics.description: Grantees receive grants worth $300,000, paid out over the course of 3 years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Financial terms: a total of $300,000 per award, disbursed over three years.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program funding and administration
rubrics_metrics.description: The program is funded through the Chicago Community Trust and administered by the Kinship Foundation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Historical/funding context: the award was established in 1980 by donations from trusts established by John G. Searle and Frances C. Searle; administration and funding bodies are specified.
